content:
Sasha: Heads-up — the GemmaX vocab conversion run produced a reordered special-token block, and a downstream quantized bring-up shows embedding misalignment.
Maya: Saw a small but consistent perf hit on our eval suite (2-3% PPL reg). Is that what you're seeing?
Hank: Yep. Quick peek at tokenizer ids shows order mismatch. tokenizer.ids[:12] -> [0, 50256, 1, 2, ...] but model config expects BOS=1, EOS=2.
Oliver: That sounds like a mapping / preserve-order issue in the converter rather than a model file problem.
Sasha: Agreed. Converter used preserve_order=false by default for that model family. That flips how special tokens are appended vs inserted.
Maya: Can you paste the exact command you ran?
Sasha: ```bash
python tools/convert_vocab.py \
  --src models/gemmax/spm.model \
  --out data/gemmax_vocab.json \
  --preserve-order false \
  --special-map default
```
Hank: Try with --preserve-order true and explicitly pass --special-map '{"bos":1,"eos":2,"unk":0}'. That fixed a similar issue for Mistral conversion.
Maya: I reran quick quantized eval (int8) after forcing preserve-order=true. Small improvements:
```
model: gemmax-alpha-int8
perplexity: 12.9
baseline_fp16: 12.8
rouge-l: 38.2 -> 38.5
```
Maya: Not perfect but within noise.
Oliver: We should also check the tokenization pipeline: are we inserting BOS token before passing to the model or relying on model-side BOS? Off-by-one here will shift rotary/pos indexing.
Sasha: Found the root cause: our HF-compatible tokenizer was adding an explicit BOS (id 50256) in the front, while GemmaX reference runtime assumes sequence starts without explicit BOS and uses position=0 for the first token. When we feed explicit BOS, the kv-cache + rotary projection ends up misaligned.
Hank: Oof. That explains why the regression looked bigger on long-context benchmarks. Rotary is sensitive to position offsets.
Maya: Quick patch idea: strip leading BOS in tokenization step for converter outputs OR remap BOS id to model's expected id. Which is cleaner?
Oliver: Stripping is lowest-risk for now. Remapping requires ensuring downstream tokenizers and detokenizers agree.
Sasha: Filed PR #912: "gemmax: strip explicit BOS on vocab convert + unit test". Patch includes a test that tokenizes a set and compares kvcache positions.
ci-bot: deploy-bot: conversion-run-1790302467 finished with warnings: 2 tokens out-of-order, automated fix applied.
Hank: I'll run the full eval on dedicated tonight (slot 3). If numbers look good, we can land the patch and rerun quantization knobs (per-channel vs per-tensor).
Maya: Also flagging to QA: check instruction-following samples and long-context summarization — rotary shifts hit hallucination rate.
Oliver: Heads-up to infra: if you see an uptick in small L1 cache misses, it's probably from recompiled int8 kernels after we re-quantize.
Sasha: Thanks all. Follow-ups: (1) Hank runs overnight eval, (2) Maya/QA do sample checks, (3) Sasha lands PR after green tests.
Oliver: :thumbsup:
Maya: ping @Hank when evals complete.
Hank: Will do.
